2026-08-30.4: Added the hand-authored terminal_outcomes top-level block (issue infiquetra/infiquetra-sdlc#90): the versioned terminal-outcome contract (R72, R73). Five dispositions each map to one of GitHub's three live closure reasons (delivered to COMPLETED; the four non-delivery dispositions duplicate, superseded, declined, canceled to the non-completed set) with the disposition itself recorded separately in the durable closeout comment, because GitHub carries three reasons and the policy names five dispositions. The replacement link for a duplicate or superseded issue rides the one durable closeout comment posted strictly before the close - markIssueAsDuplicate no longer exists in GitHub's mutation set and closeIssue(duplicateIssueId:) links and closes in the SAME call, so it cannot carry the 'before' ordering (passed additively, never load-bearing). Work that may realistically resume is never closed under any reason; may_resume.status_values is the literal UNKNOWN because no Deferred or Parked Status option exists in workflows.stage_flow or cross_cutting_statuses (X1 Inventory C recorded the identical gap). One exactly-once closeout comment carries the seven EE6 contents (delivered revision, environment, acceptance results, residual risks and follow-ups, documentation status, cleanup confirmation, closure reason), links rather than duplicates the authoritative evidence, and never fabricates an environment, deployment record, or acceptance result. Parent closure defaults to auto_close when all required child outcomes are terminal, combined verification is complete, and Retro is complete or not required, with descoped children excluded and the operator asked only on one of three named ambiguities - ambiguity is the trigger, never the default posture (R73). The predicate wire formats (descoped marker, combined-verification signal) stay W1's (#82); their pointer is parent_closure.predicate_wire_formats_resolved_by. Prose authority: docs/process/terminal-outcomes.md; oracle: tools/docs/tests/test_terminal_outcome_contract.py. Strictly additive: every other top-level block is unchanged.

description: Canonical Infiquetra SDLC board, team, routing, review, approval, and deployment-state schema. This file intentionally contains no live GitHub Projects field option IDs; tooling must resolve those from GitHub at runtime.

operations.role: Sole human operator, intent source, approval gate, escalation arbitrator, and occasional direct implementer with local AI tools

asgard.role: Jeff-proximal rapid-action, incubation, and mission-mode team with an issue-backed feed and lightweight proof model
asgard.modes_note: These three modes are an Asgard operating concept (docs/process/asgard-operating-model.md), not a project field. The Mode single-select was deleted from the Asgard board on 2026-08-16; nothing records a card's mode on the board any more.

olympus.role: Former primary autonomous engineering execution pipeline. Preserved for history only; do not route active work or current board state through Mount Olympus.

hermes.role: Hermes Agent framework and neutral capability contract used by active teams; distinct from the retired Team Hermes repository and its former plan-phase authority

team-hermes.role: Former Olympus-era plan-phase crew and deployment authority. Its remote repository is preserved, but it is not an active team or runtime owner.

themis.role: Former PR-review state machine. Preserved for migration history only; not an active routing path.

operations.name: Operations
operations.purpose: Raw operator intent, approvals, questions, personal/operator work, and shaping before team execution

asgard.name: Asgard
asgard.purpose: Rapid action, incubation, and mission-mode work close to Jeff

campps.name: CAMPPS
campps.purpose: Portfolio-level execution board for the CAMPPS program, tracking Outcome, Capability, and Component slice progress while the initiative is active
campps.archive_trigger: Operator declares the initiative complete after Objectives are Done and Outcome Scorecards are reviewed.

stage_flow.note: R66 (board-stage migration W13): Stage is the board column field; Status carries the in-stage condition. The per-stage sets below are the authoritative structured fact; the retired names Idea, Ready and Done do not survive as Status values anywhere.
stage_flow.entry_option_rule: The first name in each stage_statuses list is the entry option: defaulting there invents no recorded progress (R49). Ready for Active (Planning) and Ready to close (Verify/Retro) are terminal exceptions that preserve recorded progress.
stage_flow.status_scoping: A GitHub single-select field cannot scope options per stage, so each board's Status field carries the flat 26-option union and the per-stage sets are authoritative only here. No defensive mechanism blocks a manual out-of-stage choice (R42); consistency is descriptive.

campps_initiative.retirement_note: Former CAMPPS-only lightweight ladder. Migrated onto intent_flow on 2026-08-16: Committed -> Ready (145 cards), Parked -> Idea (49 cards), In Progress removed (0 cards). The statuses array is preserved so historical cards, plans, and reviews naming these columns remain resolvable; it does not describe any live board.

work_hierarchy.source_note: Canonical machine-readable hierarchy for the Objective, Outcome and Capability roles, plus the structural meaning of Component in the components block below. Component is NOT one of these roles and never was a legitimate one: it is an architectural and structural concept - a named part of a larger system - that an issue may name as scope metadata, never a dispatch role and never an issue type (E7, operator decision 2026-09-06, which closed the graduation hypothesis permanently and superseded the 2026-06-17 role-plus-field decision).

objective.supporting_artifact: Outcome Scorecard doc in the owning context-library repository
objective.membership_rule: Assign the Objective field value to every contributing Capability and executable child; do not create an Objective parent issue.

outcome.purpose: Dated proof tier for initiative-level outcomes when a long-lived initiative board exists.

capability.parent_policy: Top-level by default; use an Outcome parent only when the active board contract explicitly requires dated proof cards.
capability.purpose: Coordinates the end-to-end result across services and names the verification slice that proves completion.

components.source_note: Component is a structural concept, not a role and not an issue type (E7, operator decision 2026-09-06). A component is a named part of a larger system or product - a service, a repository, a module, a subsystem, or another bounded part - and it need not be independently deployable: CAMPPS identity and authorization are components, and Talaria and Auralis each contain components that are not separate AWS services. Issues keep the three-value issue-type axis and may name the component they affect as scope metadata (a "Component: <name>" line in the issue body), never as a type; an application's component list lives with that application's architecture decisions. This key was named component_slices and described Component as a repo-bounded dispatch slice under a Capability; that framing is retired, and so are the four measures the closed hypothesis watched (slice_rework_rate, dispatch_without_clarification_rate, service_test_pass_rate, cross_service_e2e_pass_rate), which are withdrawn rather than collected. What survives below is the verification doctrine - how work on a component proves itself - and the historical record of the deleted Test Strategy board field.
components.retired_field_record: Deleted from CAMPPS (Project #4) on 2026-08-16, destroying 284 field values. It had been verified live earlier the same day (single-select, options endpoint/event/schema/property/combine, 284 of 831 cards carrying a value; source tools/board/snapshot.py capture project-4-20260816T040238), and that capture is the snapshot of record at ~/.infiquetra/board-snapshots/. The five strategies below remain the verification doctrine for Component slices; only the board field that recorded the choice is gone. A slice now declares its strategy in the issue body.

endpoint.proof_expectation: Request and response seam proof for one endpoint vertical.

event.proof_expectation: Event emission, idempotency, state transition, and alarm or retry proof.

schema.proof_expectation: Schema invariant, compatibility, and generated artifact proof.

property.proof_expectation: Property, exhaustiveness, or state-space proof for non-enumerable behavior.

combine.proof_expectation: Cross-repository or cross-service seam proof that local green checks did not miss the end-to-end result.

components.capability_close_rule: Every Capability coordinator names one enforced end-to-end verification slice before close; use combine when a cross-repo seam exists or a dedicated closeout E2E slice otherwise.

parent_stage_derivation.source_note: Hand-authored (W1, issue infiquetra/infiquetra-sdlc#82). The single expression of the parent-issue Stage derivation (R5): consumers read this block and evaluate it, they never vendor or reimplement the algorithm. The one reference interpreter is tools/docs/parent_stage.py. The derivation returns exactly one Stage and never a Status: a parent's Status is derived independently of any child's (R4), and the derivation never returns the furthest Stage a child reached (R2).
parent_stage_derivation.chosen_by: docs/reviews/2026-08-29-x5-findings.md section 10 (issue #79, CLOSED/COMPLETED); adopted verbatim, not re-derived

stage_order.note: The six accepted Stages, least advanced first; pinned by membership against workflows.stage_flow.stages at load time, and a resolver raises if the two disagree.

open_child_filter.note: A required child contributes its Stage only while it is open and not explicitly descoped (R3); a terminal disposition is not part of the remaining work the parent shows.

selection.non_empty_rule: least-advanced-open-child: return the least advanced Stage in stage_order occupied by any open required child (a selection from stages actually occupied, never the furthest child reached)

fallback_arms.reason: The parent's own most recent combined-verification attempt failed and has not yet progressed back toward re-verification (R65/AE27 applied to the parent by its own 'the issue' wording; X5 section 3 arm 1). Checked ahead of the Retro arm: a failed verification is independently a Retro trigger (R8), so the two co-occur, and the parent is being repaired right now, not yet in Retro.
The parent's own Retro trigger fired and the Retro has not completed (R7-R13, evaluated at the parent; X5 section 3 arm 2).

No open required child, no failure, no Retro trigger outstanding: the parent's own combined-verification proof (P9) is pending or in progress. Closed is not a Stage (P2); whether the parent closes is decided separately (P12), never by this function.

selection.purity_note: All three fallback arms read only the parent's CURRENT recorded state, never a remembered prior Stage, so the function is pure and cross-consumer deterministic (R1); X5 section 5b rejects the stateful ratchet reading.

required_children_roster.input: Each required child carries its Stage plus one of three dispositions, natively distinguished by GitHub issue state, adding no vocabulary anywhere.

incomplete.note: Open and still linked as a required sub-issue. Also matches state_reason reopened (closed once, reopened - still open work).

completed.note: Closed as done; not part of the remaining work the parent shows. Tokens are the GraphQL IssueStateReason values; REST carries the lowercase spellings, and disposition comparison is case-normalized so the two surfaces match.

descoped.note: Explicitly descoped (R3): closed as not planned while remaining linked as a sub-issue, so the descoping is a deliberate, authored, timestamped act that stays auditable. Severing the sub-issue link instead is the silent removal R39 rejects. Excluded from the derivation inputs and distinguishable from incomplete.

own_verification_failed.semantics: The parent's own most recent combined-verification attempt failed and has not yet progressed back toward re-verification (X5 section 3 arm 1). All fallback arms read only the parent's current recorded state, never a remembered prior Stage.

instant_of_failure_token.note: The set itself is W13's authority (workflows.stage_flow.stage_statuses.Verify); the pin fails the moment 'Verification failed' leaves that set. A bare literal copy with no membership check would be a second copy of W13's vocabulary under this key. The token names the instant of failure only: R65/AE27 then move the Stage to Active, and Repairing must NOT be read as carrying this signal (R66 uses it generically for other Active-stage fixups, AE37).

repair_window_encoding.resolved_by: Operator decision E9 (2026-09-06), recorded in docs/engineering-journal/narratives/2026-09-06-sdlc-documentation-decision-record.md and landed by unit U6 of docs/plans/2026-09-07-sdlc-documentation-update-plan.md. This block no longer defers the encoding: the marker below IS the encoding, and it replaces the UNKNOWN X5 section 11 left.
repair_window_encoding.present_while: The repair window is open - that is, from the moment the parent's own verification failed until a later deployed version passes every prescribed scenario.
repair_window_encoding.writer: The Delivery Manager, through the lifecycle integration. No acting role writes it, and no consumer sets it as a side effect of reading.

events.set: When the Delivery Manager records the parent's Status as Verification failed, citing the failing test result that caused it.
events.clear: Only after a later deployed version passes every prescribed scenario, citing that passing result. Nothing else clears it.

repair_window_encoding.reader_rule: own_verification_failed is true exactly while the marker is present. Consumers READ the marker; they never re-derive the boolean from a Status. Repairing in particular carries no signal (R66 uses it generically for other Active-stage fixups, AE37), which is precisely why a durable marker was needed: the instant-of-failure token above names the instant only, and R65/AE27 move the Stage on immediately after it.
repair_window_encoding.why_a_label: The window is a fact about the parent, so it belongs on the parent's own record. A label is the cheapest durable encoding the one interpreter can read with the inputs it already has: no fourth board field, no new Status, and no parsing of prose. It does not violate the rule that no label encodes a Stage or Status value (W13 AE24), because repair-window is neither a Stage name nor a Status name - tools/docs/check_label_vocabulary.py checks exactly that.
repair_window_encoding.closing_version_rule: The two events are D2's closing-version rule stated once: closure requires every prescribed scenario passed on the closing version, so the marker's truth and the closure rule cannot disagree.
repair_window_encoding.interpreter: tools/docs/parent_stage.py labels_signal_repair_window() is the one runtime reading of the marker name; no consumer copies the literal.

retro_triggered.semantics: The parent's own Retro trigger has fired and the Retro has not completed (R7-R13, evaluated at the parent; X5 section 3 arm 2).
retro_triggered.encoding: Resolved by W2 (issue infiquetra/infiquetra-sdlc#83, which landed the retro_trigger contract): the wire input is the parent's own fired-trigger set, evaluated by tools/docs/retro_trigger.py's resolve() against signal records gathered from the parent issue's card timeline and the target repository's rollback tags, plus any operator assertion of meaningful_surprise or significant_lesson recorded at closeout. retro_triggered is true when any machine-detectable trigger fires or the operator asserts one of the two operator-asserted triggers. Tests still supply the boolean explicitly as a fixture-level input - no evaluator exists (retro_trigger.evaluator.exists is false), so no consumer derives the boolean automatically yet.

parent_stage_derivation.unknown_or_absent_inputs: raise, never default - an out-of-vocabulary Stage, an absent Stage, or an unrecognized disposition is a contract question a human answers (HALT over degrade, verify_entry.py posture). How a consumer surfaces the exception is the consumer's decision.

pause_states.source_note: Vocabulary of pause reasons, NOT a list of board columns. As of 2026-08-16 no active board carries a pause column at all: CAMPPS's Parked was the last one and was migrated into Idea. Needs Review and Needs Question are retired Mount Olympus column names kept as vocabulary. Blocked is NOT a pause state here: since the 2026-08-29 Stage migration it is a live cross-cutting Status, available in any Stage rather than belonging to one (R66). A paused card on an active board is expressed by labels and issue state. Parked is retired as a duplicate term and is NOT a live pause reason: it survives only in workflows.campps_initiative.pause_states, the retired CAMPPS ladder's historical record, so historical cards naming that column stay resolvable (E4, operator decision 2026-09-06, corrected 2026-09-07).
pause_states.Plan-Approved: Plan accepted but operator intentionally paused dispatch.
pause_states.Needs Review: Operator or team review needed before work can continue.
pause_states.Needs Question: Author or operator input needed; currently treated as a human-input state.
pause_states.Deferred: The operator deliberately paused work that may resume. A reason, never a Status: the item stays open carrying the cross-cutting Status Blocked plus the config/labels.json label pause/operator-deferred, and the reason text and the resume condition go in the comment that sets Blocked. A pause expected to outlast the current planning horizon routes to the External / Deferred destination with its Stage and reason intact; resuming clears the reason and routes back. Metrics count deferred time separately from ordinary blocked time, and a deliberate pause never trips a stalled-work alert (E4).

rule.applies_to: every board that uses workflows.stage_flow and dispatches Active work
rule.note: adding a board binds it; no per-board policy

Ready: Issue body satisfies the card contract (docs/process/card-schema.md), enforced by mission-control at creation
Outcome or Capability is admitted to the initiative portfolio

planning_to_active_readiness.source_note: Hand-authored per the W3 plan (issue infiquetra/infiquetra-sdlc#84), generalized by operator decision E3 (2026-09-06), recorded in docs/engineering-journal/narratives/2026-09-06-sdlc-documentation-decision-record.md and landed by unit U6 of docs/plans/2026-09-07-sdlc-documentation-update-plan.md. The single organization-wide Planning-to-Active readiness rule (R14): operations.Active, asgard.Active and campps.Active all reference this one rule object rather than carrying per-team checklists, and no per-team checklist may be introduced to fill the gap. Which boards are bound is stated once in dispatch_gates.rule, not board by board: a board qualifies when it uses this schema's workflows.stage_flow vocabulary AND dispatches Active work, and inherited_by_contract means a future qualifying board is bound without a policy decision, a bespoke checklist, or any edit beyond joining that rule's bound list. Each board's creation-time Ready gate is a different gate at a different boundary and stays distinct. The one reference interpreter is tools/docs/planning_readiness.py; a consumer evaluates this block, never reimplements it.
planning_to_active_readiness.description: Evidence-sufficiency test for entry to Active from Planning (R15). The decision is computed from the card body alone - the projection reads the committed schema and the parsed card and nothing else: no board, no API, no environment - so an ordinary item always yields a decision with no operator input.

C1.statement: The intended outcome and acceptance expectations are understandable.
C1.note: All four are always-required core fields (issue_fields.required_matrix rules[0]); every conforming card carries them, so C1 evaluates on an ordinary item with nothing to ask.

C2.statement: Important dependencies and ownership are actionable.
C2.note: context_library_links is required-or-the declared _none_ sentinel: the sentinel means knowingly none and satisfies C2, a card missing the field entirely does not. Ownership and dependency structure (assignee, parent/sub-issue links) come from the same issue fetch as the body.

C3.statement: Any genuinely required design decision is settled.
C3.note: lifecycle_origin must name a /plan artifact; it is auto-populated, not author-required, so C3 still needs no operator input. A literal UNKNOWN token remaining in the body marks an unsettled decision: the repository's card-contract affordance makes UNKNOWN a first-class honest answer that routes to the operator, so a card carrying one is correctly not ready for Active.

C4.statement: The threshold scales with context and risk.
C4.note: The only risk-conditional condition: the three fields it deepens are exactly the three issue_fields.required_matrix marks risk-conditional, and their requiredness depends on the card's own risk value. That value now has one defined source, the issue_fields.fields.risk card-contract field added by operator decision E1 (2026-09-06), so C4 is evaluated rather than refused (see risk_scaling.source). A card whose risk value is absent, or still reads the literal UNKNOWN token, fails C4 and routes to the operator; the rule never defaults to a tier (R17, AE16).

baseline_threshold.note: The three conditions every card must satisfy whatever its risk tier. With risk scaling enabled (operator decision E1, 2026-09-06) the rule adds C4 on top of this baseline and does assert a risk tier - the one the card itself carries - so asserts_no_risk_tier is false. The baseline is still the whole demand at the lean tiers, because issue_fields.required_matrix leaves the risk-conditional trio optional at low and medium, and it is never relaxed: a higher tier only ever adds C4's evidence, it never removes a baseline condition.

risk_scaling.source: issue_fields.fields.risk - the fourteenth card-contract field, added by operator decision E1 (2026-09-06). The tier is read from the card body and nowhere else: the risk: labels in config/labels.json stay a board projection written by the lifecycle integration, never a source, and no board field carries the value.
risk_scaling.effect: C4 is evaluated against the card's own risk value. Which tiers deepen the three fields below is resolved by reading issue_fields.required_matrix, so this block writes no tier name of its own and cannot drift from the matrix. An absent risk value, or one still reading the literal UNKNOWN token, fails C4 and routes to the operator; the rule never defaults to a tier (R17, AE16).
risk_scaling.deepens_how: The same three fields issue_fields.required_matrix marks risk-conditional. The matrix is the single source of which tiers require them: the reference interpreter tools/docs/planning_readiness.py resolves each field against the matrix for the card's tier rather than carrying a second copy of the policy.
risk_scaling.schema_validity_rule: risk_scaling.enabled true requires a risk supplier: issue_fields.fields must carry a field keyed risk and issue_fields.required_matrix.axes.field must list it. A schema that enables scaling without one is malformed, and tools/docs/planning_readiness.py fails its schema validation with a plain error naming the missing field rather than scaling against a value nothing supplies.

design_record.normal: The /plan artifact is the normal design record (R18).
design_record.note: A separate design document is produced only on a named trigger below, never by default. The trigger is scope/complexity-shaped, deliberately not a risk tier: no risk tier is available to key on, and R18's complexity trigger must not smuggle in the risk dependency R17 forbids.

triggers.statement: The change spans multiple services, so planning evidence must include a separate design document and a diagram.
triggers.example: A change spanning four services produces both a separate design document and a diagram.

separate_design_doc_triggers.note: The trigger list contains no risk-tier token by construction, so the separate-design-document decision cannot become a risk-scaled rule keyed to an input with no defined source.

diagram_rule.rule: Include a diagram when the approach has shape prose alone does not carry; skip it when the approach is a one-paragraph pattern application.
diagram_rule.implemented_by: skills/plan/references/plan-sections.md (the Saga /plan skill's High-Level Technical Design section rule) - the policy is encoded here once and cited to its implementer.

applicability_scan.domain_source: config/lens-catalogue.json - the lens identifiers of the universal lens catalogue. The scan's domains ARE the catalogue's lenses; there is no separate domain list (operator decision E2).
applicability_scan.domain_source_note: The undefined fixed count of eight domains is retired. A second list of concerns beside the catalogue would be a rival concern vocabulary, which is exactly what decision E2 forbids: 'the universal lens catalogue is the single concern vocabulary'. The fixture domain list the refusing form was tested over is retired with it - the rule is now tested over the catalogue's real lens identifiers.
applicability_scan.declared_when: during planning, once per work unit
applicability_scan.declaration: For each work unit the Planner declares which catalogue lenses apply and which do not, with a reason for each non-applicable one, and decomposes the work, constraints, checks, and evidence to reach the quality the applicable lenses require.
applicability_scan.always_on_lenses_are_not_declarable: A lens the catalogue marks always_on is applicable by the catalogue and is never declared away; the declaration covers the conditional lenses only.
applicability_scan.recorded_reason_rule: Every domain in the scan either applies to the change under planning or carries a brief recorded reason why it does not apply - the recorded reason, never an empty section, is what satisfies the check for a non-applicable domain (R19).
applicability_scan.boundary: Planning for review readiness, not staffing and not scoring. The Planner chooses no vendor, model, executor, effort, score, or outcome; the Delivery Manager resolves staffing and freezes the run's roster afterwards, and Code Review judges independently (operator decision E2).
consumed_by: the Planning-to-Active readiness evidence, as the planning half
tools/docs/gen_review_roster.py, as the run's applicability declaration when the roster is resolved
applicability_scan.effect: Enabled. A work unit whose plan carries no declaration, or whose declaration names a lens identifier absent from the catalogue, or leaves a non-applicable lens without a recorded reason, does not satisfy the planning-evidence condition.

bindings.governed_by: dispatch_gates.rule - the generic binding. The three entries below record where each current board's Active gate resolves; they are the rule's bound list made concrete, not three separate policies.
bindings.asgard_active: dispatch_gates.asgard.Active -> this rule (was the UNKNOWN placeholder)
bindings.campps_active: dispatch_gates.campps.Active -> this rule (was the UNKNOWN placeholder)
bindings.operations_active: dispatch_gates.operations.Active -> this rule. Bound by operator decision E3 (2026-09-06), which generalized readiness to every board that uses the shared lifecycle and dispatches active work; the W3 plan's UNKNOWN-3 is closed by that decision. The Operations Ready gate above is unchanged: it is the creation-time card-contract check, a different gate at a different boundary.

planning_to_active_readiness.result_note: Readiness is represented as the Ready for Active Status inside Planning (R16); the vocabulary was provisioned by W13 (issue #94) and is not re-provisioned here. No bare Ready status exists in workflows.stage_flow and no Ready column is reintroduced on any board.

team_routing.operations_ready_rule: A Ready Operations card must satisfy the card contract before moving to another board or workflow. Routing to a surface is an explicit operator action, not a field value.
team_routing.asgard_issue_feed_rule: Asgard-bound work enters by an operator routing an Operations card to Asgard, a direct issue added to Asgard, or a context/issue pack. The former pre-Active field checklist (Mode, target repository or surface, risk, approval state, proof path, transfer target) is void: every field backing it was deleted from the board on 2026-08-16. Mode, target surface, risk, and transfer intent now live in the issue body per the card contract (docs/process/card-schema.md), not in project fields.
team_routing.cross_team_transfer_rule: Asgard and CAMPPS are sibling active target surfaces. Cross-team movement happens only when an operator explicitly routes, transfers, clones, or links work to another board; readiness checks may warn about target fit but must not infer movement. Mount Olympus is retired historical context and is not an active target.
team_routing.default_pressure_valve: Prefer project views over new boards unless scale, automation, or reporting needs justify a separate board.

review_model.team_owned_review: The team that owns the work owns PR review, evidence, and merge readiness. Hermes may coordinate events, but does not route active PR review to Themis.
review_model.plan_review: Hermes can coordinate plan review before dispatch.
review_model.publication_lane: The Saga Code Review publication lane, granted in interactive / standalone mode only: the reviewer may write, commit, and push its own review document and submit the GitHub pull-request review. The lane grants no implementation-edit authority over reviewed source and is bounded to the review artifact's own path (docs/code-reviews/ plus the evidence ledger under docs/evidence/). A review-artifact commit is evidence only and records the exact implementation revision reviewed as a full 40-character commit SHA in the artifact frontmatter (reviewed_revision). Programmatic / report-only mode keeps its zero-durable-writes contract, which the Work staleness gate depends on.
review_model.repair_custody: The reviewer does not implement the fixes it requests. Findings route to the author or the Work process, which own repair changes and implementation commits.
review_model.implementation_route_note: Q6 answer, decided 2026-08-28: granting the lane requires no new registered operation kind in the safety allowlist and no widening of an existing one. The plugin's OpKind registry mirrors mission-control verbs, intentionally excludes repo-level mutations, and is default-deny, so the lane is bounded by the skill contract and the reviewer's toolset. Recorded with rationale in docs/engineering-journal/DECISIONS.md.

retired.Themis: Historical PR-review state machine. Do not route active PR review to Themis from current SDLC docs.
retired.Proceed__Revise__Block verdict vocabular: The earlier three-way review verdict vocabulary is retired (source requirement R76, issue #99). Live documents express review results with the real Saga counterpart's vocabulary: the four typed review_result.v1 outcomes for PR review, and the one-line readiness verdict plus P0-P3 finding priorities for plan review. Historical use survives only in dated records (brainstorms, ideation notes, reviews).

human_approval_state.active_pattern: Per-agent direct message or per-card thread request to the operator, depending on the work context.
approval_required_for: major team or process authority changes

lifecycle_field_mutation.writable_fields_note: The single constrained Mission Control lifecycle-field mutation may write only these two fields; any other field name is rejected before a board is touched. Authored contract, not read at runtime: the plugin enforces its own CORRECTION_FIELDS literal.
lifecycle_field_mutation.allowed_submissions_note: The one list of phase-boundary moves a caller may submit through this mutation. It is the single authority: docs/process/lifecycle-field-mutation.md and docs/process/saga-board-write-authority.md both render this list as a generated region, so the two chapters cannot state different rules. Before plan decision Q79 (2026-09-07) each chapter carried its own hand-authored table, one with five rows and one with six, and both claimed to be the single authority on board writes (fresh-eyes round 7, finding 2). Every Stage and Status below is a value workflows.stage_flow already declares; tools/docs/gen_lifecycle_docs.py fails the render rather than printing a pair the flow does not carry.
lifecycle_field_mutation.allowed_submissions_ready_to_close_note: **Six rows, not five.** `Ready to close` is carried under both Verify and Retro because Stage plus Status is the key. `retro_trigger.no_trigger_closure` in `config/sdlc-schema.json` says a run with no fired trigger closes directly from Verify and never enters Retro, so a delivered terminal reached without a trigger is submitted under Verify, and one reached after Retro is submitted under Retro. The two rows are the two ends of one branch, not a conflict.

allowed_submissions.when: After merge and the applicable delivery or artifact verification
At a delivered terminal where the closure conditions hold and no Retro trigger fired
At a delivered terminal after Retro, where a trigger did fire

lifecycle_field_mutation.board_discovery_note: Carrying boards are resolved from the issue's own projectItems, never from a repo-to-board mapping.
lifecycle_field_mutation.atomicity_note: Either every board carrying the issue ends at the new value, or every board ends at the value it held before the call.
lifecycle_field_mutation.transition_legality_note: No Stage or Status ladder exists and none may be added: no transition is rejected because an intermediate value was never occupied, backward movement is permitted whenever it truthfully represents current activity with the reason recorded, and no reconcile pass back-fills an unoccupied value.

gate_catalogue.source_note: Hand-authored per the W4 plan (issue infiquetra/infiquetra-sdlc#85). Membership is X7's 44-row working set plus the three deploy-plugin rows, transcribed row-by-row from the census. Classification enum: advisory (the default), blocking (only where the gate's own contract names mandatory evidence or a safety boundary), and the explicit string unclassified (the gate pauses for an operator decision - it never silently blocks and never silently advances). Every blocking row's classification_basis opens with the P14 trigger that justifies it ("Mandatory evidence:" or "Safety boundary:"); an unclassified row's classification_basis records why no verdict could be reached.

planning_to_active.note: All three are blocking, classified from the evidence of the one rule they share, dispatch_gates.planning_to_active_readiness (operator decision E3, 2026-09-06). The list enumerates the boards bound TODAY; which boards qualify is stated once in dispatch_gates.rule, and a future qualifying board is bound by that rule and joins this list without a new policy decision. approval_boundary_safety.note: P22 categories mapped: production changes (production-deployment-safety, deploy-autonomy-posture, deploy F1-F3), destructive actions and external commitments and changes to process authority (no-force-push, outward-github-mutation-confirmation, automation-eligibility-gate, tier-escalation-confirmation). These nine gates are the enforcement points that already exist; they are not the whole boundary map. E8 (operator decision 2026-09-06, briefing 41a) settled the rest: all seven approval categories are minimal AUTHORITY BOUNDARIES, and each one is recorded - with the scope a grant must name, the actions that always exceed it, and the evidence that the boundary held - in gate_catalogue.approval_boundaries, which reads the category list from human_approval_state.approval_required_for by name rather than copying it. A category whose only test is whether the operator authorized this specific action is a boundary, and its evidence is the authorization record, not a six-attribute pass/fail gate; no gate is minted for credentials and identity or for material spending, and minting one would edit human_approval_state and invent contracts. The W4 plan's UNKNOWN-2, which recorded those two categories as a known gap, is RETIRED on that reading. The one remaining mechanical question - whether a secrets scanner joins the organization's binding toolchain standard - belongs to infiquetra-context-library as the standards owner; if that standard names one, a genuine mechanical gate joins this catalogue then, and not before.

approval_boundaries.source_note: The seven approval categories are minimal AUTHORITY BOUNDARIES on what a run may do, not seven automatic per-action interruptions (E8, operator decision 2026-09-06 on briefing 41a). The category list is NOT copied here: it is read from human_approval_state.approval_required_for, and every key of categories below is one of that list's exact strings. A run acts within the authority the operator recorded for that work item at orchestration setup, category by category and with named scope; an action inside the recorded scope proceeds with no further prompt, and only an action that would exceed it stops and returns to the operator with the specific decision. This block records what a grant must name, what always exceeds it, and the evidence a boundary held; it mints no gate and grants no authority.

absolute_invariants.note: Outside the authorization system entirely: no recorded grant can include them, no gate overrides them, and no role may act against one under any authority.
invariants: never force-push a protected or default branch

always_exceeds: a production promotion not already named in an approved promotion record
approval_boundaries.unscoped_grant_rule: A grant without named scope is not a boundary but a missing one. A role that meets an unscoped grant reports a blocker under B2 rather than acting on it. The operator grants the scope; the Delivery Manager records it in the run setup record and allocates it to roles, and can never widen it.
approval_boundaries.evidence_rule: A boundary held when the recorded grant covers the action and the action left its own durable record - a deployment record, a spend record, a merge - and, at the edge of the grant, the operator's decision on the issue. A reviewer treating an action as authorized cites the grant that covers it.
approval_boundaries.enforcement_points: The nine gates listed under floor_gates.approval_boundary_safety are the pass/fail enforcement points that already exist; that block's note records which categories they serve. Categories without such a gate are enforced by the acting role stopping and the Delivery Manager escalating.

verify_entry.description: Single authority for the Active/Verify boundary: the condition under which a work item may enter Verify, and whether a check belongs to Active or Verify. Prose documents link here and must not restate this contract (R10).
verify_entry.resolver_note: Resolved by tools/docs/verify_entry.py for reviewers and any automated consumer. The Stage write itself is W6's constrained Mission Control mutation; the causing-evidence inventory is X1's audit.
verify_entry.evidence_audit: docs/reviews/2026-08-29-x1-findings.md Inventory A transition T5 (Active -> Verify)
verify_entry.causing_evidence: For work with deployable software: a merged change plus a succeeded non-production deployment record. For work with no deployable software: the delivered artifact existing in its real form in the consumption context that must be evaluated. None of these may be fabricated (R71/EE8).
verify_entry.recording_operation: Mission Control's constrained lifecycle-field mutation (W6's authored contract, landed 2026-08-28): one atomic all-carrying-boards-or-none Stage/Status write resolving carrying boards from the issue's own projectItems. Today's live mechanism is `flow set-field --correction` reached through the reconcile controller's set-field-status op. Verify is never written pre-merge (X1 audit, Central Mechanism; T5).

deployable_work.note: Verify is entered only after merge plus a succeeded non-production deployment. A failed or missing deployment leaves the item in Active (R69).

pre_merge_stays_active.note: Pre-merge CI, tests, code review, and PR-ready never advance the Stage to Verify (R69/R2).

no_deployable_software.require_merge_note: Verify begins after merge for this class of work too; the R71 no-deployable route relaxes the deployment requirement, never the merge requirement (R69/R1).
no_deployable_software.verified_when: The delivered artifact exists in the real form and consumption context that must be evaluated: the rendered published page for documentation, the installed version for a plugin (R71/R6).

deploying_to_non_production.never_set_when: the work has no deployable software

no_deployable_software.note: Where deployment practice does not apply, the absence is recorded with a reason; no environment or deployment record may be fabricated to satisfy the transition (R71, EE8).

test_placement.description: Whether a check belongs to Active or Verify, keyed on its target and timing -- never on the label 'end-to-end' (R70/R5). A check whose target is an assembled candidate (an artifact built from the change, not yet deployed) at pre-merge or at-merge timing is Active; a check whose target is a deployed environment or the delivered artifact in its consumption context at post-deployment timing is Verify.

targets.assembled_candidate: An artifact built from the change (repository checkout, built/installed-from-source candidate) that has not been deployed to an environment.
targets.deployed_environment: A real (including non-production) environment the change has been deployed to.
targets.delivered_artifact_in_context: The delivered artifact in its real consumption context: the rendered published page for documentation, the installed version for a plugin.

timings.post_deployment: After the change is merged and deployed, or after the no-deployable-software artifact exists in its consumption context.

rule.unresolved: HALT: a target/timing combination the rule does not name raises rather than defaulting (HALT over degrade).

retro_trigger.description: Single authority for the conditional Retro trigger: which triggers a machine may detect, which named observable signal each is bound to, which two only the operator may assert, and what closure and the routine per-pull-request capture do regardless. Prose documents link here and must not restate this contract (R7-R13).
retro_trigger.resolver_note: Projected by tools/docs/retro_trigger.py for reviewers and any automated consumer. The resolver is pure and read-only: it evaluates trigger ids against signal records supplied to it and never fetches, polls, or observes anything on its own.

evaluator.note: No evaluator of these trigger conditions exists anywhere in the running system - not in the Saga plugin, not in any board write path. Recorded per X1 (docs/reviews/2026-08-29-x1-findings.md, transition T7, consolidated gap 9): no actor is named as the evaluator of Retro's machine-detectable trigger conditions. Each signal below is a definition a future evaluator would read, not evidence that detection happens. A consumer who needs a trigger decided must gather the signal records itself and resolve them with tools/docs/retro_trigger.py; nothing in this contract observes anything on its own (R7).

failed_verification.signal: ProjectV2ItemStatusChangedEvent on one issue's project card timeline with status == "Verification failed" (event on the boards' designated Status field, named explicitly so a future board re-designation surfaces as a contract mismatch rather than as silently wrong data)
failed_verification.source: GitHub issue timeline - Projects v2 item status-change events on the issue's card
failed_verification.read_only_query: GraphQL on the issue: timelineItems(first: 100, itemTypes: [PROJECT_V2_ITEM_STATUS_CHANGED_EVENT]) { ... on ProjectV2ItemStatusChangedEvent { previousStatus status createdAt actor wasAutomated } }; select events where status == "Verification failed"
failed_verification.observed_to_date: none - zero instances with status == "Verification failed" as of 2026-08-30
failed_verification.evidence: Probe 2026-08-30 (read-only): the event type exists in the live GraphQL schema and returns real data - four events on issue infiquetra/infiquetra-sdlc#94, the most recent "Awaiting verification" to "Ready to close" at 2026-08-30T04:06:41Z. "Verification failed" is a live Status option on all three boards (workflows.stage_flow.stage_statuses.Verify).
failed_verification.corroborating_secondary_signal: Where a Saga run produced one, the committed evidence ledger's no-ship verdict (docs/evidence/<saga-id>/ledger.jsonl) corroborates failed verification. It is not the primary signal because it exists only where a Saga run produced it, while the board event exists for every issue on every board regardless of which tooling did the work.

rollback.signal: Git tag matching rollback-<environment>-v* in the work's target repository - minted by the deploy plugin (scripts/mint_tag.py, plugin 0.2.1) at the moment a rollback is performed

rollback.read_only_query: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/matching-refs/tags/rollback - match returned ref names against rollback-<environment>-v*
rollback.observed_to_date: none - zero rollback tags in any Infiquetra repository as of 2026-08-30
rollback.evidence: Probe 2026-08-30 (read-only): the query is valid and returns a well-formed empty list. Seven Infiquetra repositories probed, including the five CAMPPS delivery repositories that carry 25-30 real deployments each; none carries a rollback-* tag. infiquetra-sdlc itself carries zero deployments and zero environments.

repeated_repair_loop.source: GitHub issue timeline - Projects v2 item status-change events on the issue's card
repeated_repair_loop.read_only_query: GraphQL on the issue: timelineItems(first: 100, itemTypes: [PROJECT_V2_ITEM_STATUS_CHANGED_EVENT]) { ... on ProjectV2ItemStatusChangedEvent { previousStatus status createdAt } }; count events where status == "Repairing"
repeated_repair_loop.threshold_note: Fires at a count of 2 or more Repairing entries on one issue (R8). One Repairing entry is an ordinary repair, not a loop.
repeated_repair_loop.observed_to_date: none - zero instances with status == "Repairing" as of 2026-08-30
repeated_repair_loop.evidence: Probe 2026-08-30 (read-only): same event shape as failed_verification. "Repairing" is a live Status option on all three boards. A status-change census across thirteen run issues found Shaping, Active, Verify, Done, and one post-migration "Ready to close" - no "Verification failed", no "Repairing".

meaningful_surprise.prompt: Was this run a meaningful surprise? If yes, say so at closeout and Retro runs on your assertion alone.

significant_lesson.prompt: Did this run produce a significant design or process lesson worth the larger retrospective? If yes, say so at closeout and Retro runs on your assertion alone.

no_trigger_closure.description: When no trigger fires, the run closes directly from Verify with no Retro stage entered (R10).

routine_capture.artifact: the five-question capture entry in the engineering journal
routine_capture.note: Runs routinely per merged pull request whether or not any Retro trigger fired (R11, P13). This capture and the engineering journal survive as cross-cutting practice; the trigger governs only the larger retrospective.

journal.append_only_note: The engineering journal (docs/engineering-journal/) is the append-only collection point for both the routine capture and the larger retrospective (R12). Corrections update entries inline with the corrected-and-archived discipline; entries are never silently overwritten.
journal.promote_note: The Saga /promote skill is manual, gated, and operator-visible: it is invoked explicitly, it proposes context-library writes as diffs that wait for approval, and no code path in any installed plugin invokes it automatically (R12). /retro's Transcendent marker waits in place for the next explicit promote run.

closure.description: The larger retrospective uses Retro's accepted Status vocabulary and closes to Closed, never to a Done column (R13, P2).
closure.vocabulary_provenance: Matches workflows.stage_flow.stage_statuses.Retro, provisioned by W13's board-stage migration and verified live on all three boards on 2026-08-30. Done no longer exists as a Status option on any active board. Sibling source: W11 (issue #92) has since landed and saga_lifecycle.phase_board_map.retro now maps the retro phase to the Retro Stage on all three boards, consistent with this block.

terminal_outcomes.status_note: The contract is authored, versioned and tested here. It is Partial because the Mission Control operation that would honour it does not exist yet - issue_close carries no reason or disposition argument and no closeout-comment poster exists (X1, Inventory E). The second reason it used to carry - that may_resume.status_values was UNKNOWN - is gone: E4 resolved that landing value to Blocked plus a pause reason on 2026-09-06.
terminal_outcomes.source: docs/brainstorms/2026-08-27-reconciled-sdlc-implementation-requirements.md (R72, R73, P10, P11, P12, EE6, EE8)
terminal_outcomes.authored_contract_note: Nothing reads this block at runtime. The plugin repository holds its own closure path; this block is the contract that work is built and reviewed against, and this repository's oracle is its only automated witness.
terminal_outcomes.github_reason_note: Verified live by GraphQL introspection of IssueClosedStateReason on 2026-08-30. GitHub carries three closure reasons; the policy names five dispositions, so a disposition is not a closure reason and is recorded separately.

replacement_link.native_argument_note: markIssueAsDuplicate no longer exists in GitHub's GraphQL mutation set (verified 2026-08-30; only unmarkIssueAsDuplicate survives). The one surviving way to mint MARKED_AS_DUPLICATE_EVENT is closeIssue(duplicateIssueId:), which links and closes in the SAME call and so cannot satisfy 'links its replacement before it closes'. The ordering obligation is discharged by the durable closeout comment, which P11 already requires posted before the close. Passing duplicateIssueId on the close is permitted and additive; it is never what makes the link 'before'.

may_resume.rule: Work that may realistically resume stays open. It is never closed, under any reason.
may_resume.status_values_note: RESOLVED by E4 (operator decision 2026-09-06, corrected 2026-09-07), replacing the literal UNKNOWN X1's audit recorded rather than fabricate a landing value (docs/reviews/2026-08-29-x1-findings.md, Inventory C). R72 asked for deferred or parked to be recorded through Status; the answer is that no Deferred and no Parked Status is created. Deliberately paused work carries the existing cross-cutting Status Blocked plus a structured pause reason from pause_states - Deferred, meaning the operator deliberately paused work that may resume - expressed on the issue by the config/labels.json label pause/operator-deferred, with the reason text and the resume condition in the comment that sets Blocked. A pause expected to outlast the current planning horizon routes to the External / Deferred destination with its Stage and reason intact rather than closing; resuming clears the reason and routes it back. Metrics count deferred time separately from ordinary blocked time and a deliberate pause never trips a stalled-work alert. The stays-open rule above is unchanged and was never conditional on this resolution.

closeout_comment.required_contents_note: closure_reason is GitHub's three-valued IssueClosedStateReason enum (COMPLETED / NOT_PLANNED / DUPLICATE); disposition is this block's five-way terminal disposition recorded in the same closeout comment. Splitting the two is the block's load-bearing rule: a reason alone can never recover superseded vs declined vs canceled from NOT_PLANNED, nor duplicate from DUPLICATE.

parent_closure.ask_operator_note: Ambiguity is the trigger for asking, not a default posture (R73). A parent meeting all three conditions with no ambiguity closes without a prompt.
parent_closure.predicate_wire_formats_note: W1 (issue infiquetra/infiquetra-sdlc#82) LANDED the child-side encodings in this same schema (see work_hierarchy.parent_stage_derivation.required_children_roster): an explicitly descoped child is CLOSED with state_reason NOT_PLANNED (GraphQL; REST lowercase, comparison case-normalized), a delivered child is CLOSED with COMPLETED, and an open required child is OPEN with reason null or reopened - so no predicate here is UNKNOWN any more on the child side, and this block never restates those tokens. The parent's own combined-verification signal remains UNKNOWN and is W1's (#82) remaining deliverable. Composition with this block's five dispositions is SETTLED by the operator's AFK ruling of 2026-08-30 (recorded durably on issue infiquetra/infiquetra-sdlc#90, R2 wave repair F-2): see duplicate_composition below.

duplicate_composition.ruling: Operator AFK ruling, 2026-08-30, issue infiquetra/infiquetra-sdlc#90: a CLOSED issue carrying the durable disposition duplicate together with its required replacement link is terminal non-delivery, and composes into W1's existing descoped category at the parent-derivation/closure boundary - justified because GitHub represents it with the non-completed closure-reason family the dispositions mapping already carries (DUPLICATE for a duplicate, NOT_PLANNED for the rest).
duplicate_composition.collapse_boundary: W1's three-value parent-derivation roster (incomplete / completed / descoped); duplicate is PRESERVED as this block's durable operator-facing closeout disposition - it is not renamed, merged away, or hidden anywhere else, and dispositions.duplicate keeps closing with GitHub's DUPLICATE reason.
duplicate_composition.not_ambiguous_when: both the durable duplicate disposition AND the required replacement link are present: the child composes to descoped and is terminal non-delivery for the parent-close conditions.
duplicate_composition.fail_closed: A missing durable disposition, or a missing required replacement link (replacement_link.required_for includes duplicate), still FAILS: the child is not counted terminal and the parent-close composition halts - terminal_disposition_ambiguous asks the operator. Fail-closed was never relaxed by the ruling.
duplicate_composition.reference_interpreter: tools/docs/parent_closure.py (compose_duplicate_into_w1); W1's classifier tools/docs/parent_stage.py is unmodified - fed a raw CLOSED/DUPLICATE it still raises, because the composition runs before the derivation sees the child.

status_definitions.source_note: Hand-authored, landing operator decision E5 (2026-09-06) recorded in docs/engineering-journal/narratives/2026-09-06-sdlc-documentation-decision-record.md, through unit U6 of docs/plans/2026-09-07-sdlc-documentation-update-plan.md, whose Appendix B is the authored source of every row below. Every lifecycle Status is defined by three things and only three: the observable event that ENTERS it, the role whose reported outcome constitutes that event, and the role or integration AUTHORIZED to write it. Nothing here re-states the Status vocabulary: workflows.stage_flow.stage_statuses stays the single authority for which Statuses exist and which Stage each belongs to, and this block is keyed by that same Stage-and-Status pair. tools/docs/gen_lifecycle_docs.py renders it into docs/process/kanban-workflow.md as the generated region status-definitions.
status_definitions.requirements_owned: E5; Q10 and Q13 of the 2026-09-07 documentation update plan
status_definitions.key_rule: Stage plus Status is the key, never Status alone. Ready to close is deliberately carried under both Verify and Retro (plan decision Q13): the two are different conditions reached from different preceding stages, and a name-keyed map could not hold both definitions. That is why this block nests under stages rather than keying on the flat workflows.stage_flow.statuses list.
status_definitions.counting_note: 26 Stage-and-Status pairs over 25 distinct Status names, because Ready to close appears twice. The flat workflows.stage_flow.statuses list holds 26 distinct names: the same 25 plus the cross-cutting Blocked, which is not one of the 26 pairs and is recorded under cross_cutting below. A rendering that appends the Blocked row to the 26 pairs therefore shows 27 rows, which is correct and is explained on the chapter.

derivation.Retro: The Retro trigger contract (retro_trigger in this schema; docs/process/learning-loop.md)

status_definitions.writer_rule: Acting roles never write their own Status. The Delivery Manager records every run transition through the lifecycle integration, and the operator or the prepared Mission Control path writes the non-run Stages. The reporting_role of a row is therefore whose OUTCOME the event is, and the writer is who records it; the two differ on purpose wherever a run role reports.
status_definitions.retirement_candidates: None. Deriving the rows found an observable entering event for every one of the 26 pairs, so no Status exists only as a name, and E5's rule that a Status without a real entering event returns to the operator as an explicit retirement candidate reports nothing here. The one naming collision, Ready to close, is reported and kept (Q13).

Capturing.entering_event: An idea, request, or question is filed as an issue

Needs clarification.entering_event: The operator or Product asks the requester a question the issue cannot proceed without

Triage.entering_event: The operator is deciding whether and where the work belongs

Discovering.entering_event: The operator and Product begin turning the idea into product content

Defining requirements.entering_event: Product content and acceptance criteria are being written; the Architect's technical context is requested

Designing.entering_event: Steps 1 and 2 begin: the Planner is dispatched

Design review.entering_event: The planner's handoff exists and plan review is dispatched

Execution planning.entering_event: Plan review returns `ready` and orchestration setup begins

Ready for Active.entering_event: The readiness rule passes and the run setup record is written

Implementing.entering_event: Step 5 begins: a worker is dispatched to a work unit

Integrating.entering_event: A work-unit branch enters its merge turn

Code review.entering_event: A review cycle is dispatched on a frozen revision

Repairing.entering_event: A review result below threshold is on the record and repair planning is dispatched

Ready to merge.entering_event: Every selected lens meets its threshold, or the exhausted path applies with no blocker

Deploying to non-production.entering_event: The Release Worker is dispatched for the merge and delivery

Awaiting verification.entering_event: Delivery succeeded and testing has not started

Verification failed.entering_event: A testing result with at least one failed scenario is on the record; the repair-window marker is set

Closeout.entering_event: Every prescribed scenario passed on the closing version; closure evaluation begins

Ready to close.entering_event: Closure conditions hold and no Retro trigger fired

Gathering evidence.entering_event: A Retro trigger fired at closure

Awaiting operator input.entering_event: An operator-asserted trigger prompt is open

Blocked.entering_event: A role reports a blocker, with the reason recorded in the comment that sets the Status
Blocked.reporting_role: The role that reports the blocker
Blocked.stage_scope: Any Stage - the card keeps the Stage it is in and carries Blocked alongside it (workflows.stage_flow.cross_cutting_statuses)
Blocked.writer: The writer for the Stage the card is in: the Delivery Manager through the lifecycle integration on a run Stage, the operator or the prepared Mission Control path otherwise
Blocked.pause_note: A pause the operator chose is this Status plus a pause reason from pause_states, carried on the issue by the single label pause/operator-deferred (decision E4)

saga_lifecycle.description: Hand-authored minimal Saga adapter (W11, issue infiquetra/infiquetra-sdlc#92): only what a confirmed consumer reads (X2 consumer audit, docs/reviews/2026-08-29-x2-findings.md section 5), plus the two versioned derivation inputs command_classification and foreign_commands (R59/R61/R68). Authored, not generated: command-to-Stage mapping is derived exclusively from phase_command_map plus command_classification, never from the vendored snapshot's commands[].phase field (R59).

saga_lifecycle.state_axes_preface: These three axes are the saga command toolkit's own stored record of one thread, not the board's: the thread status below (including `paused`) is what the tool knows about the thread and is never a board Status, while the board's own two axes — its Stage and its Status — are the ones the phase table above maps each phase onto.

doc-review.source: saga-docs-model.yaml commands.doc-review.gates ('P0/P1 findings block /work without recorded override')
doc-review.note: The authoritative check that a plan is ready to implement. An unresolved P0 or P1 finding — the two highest finding severities — stops /work until it is fixed or waived with a written reason, and clearing this gate moves the thread from review → work.

code-review.note: Today this is the quality lens the work loop runs on itself at the boundary between building and opening a pull request. It raises findings, holds no merge authority, and moves the thread to no new phase; it does not stand in for the review the owning team runs on the pull request. The run model's multi-lens code review is the target design, not what runs today.

qa.source: saga-docs-model.yaml commands.qa (saga_state_behavior: 'on pass, advances qa-track'; gates: 'Verdict threshold determines ship, ship-with-deferred, or no-ship')
qa.note: The acceptance verdict taken on the evidence after the merge. It advises the team-owned gate rather than blocking it: a passing verdict moves the thread qa → retro and records the quality-assurance track, a no-ship verdict keeps the thread in work, and ship-with-deferred is the path that ships with the reason written down.

plan-review.source: config/sdlc-schema.json review_model.plan_review ('Hermes can coordinate plan review before dispatch')
plan-review.note: Hermes coordinates this readiness check on a plan before the work is dispatched. It stops the dispatch, and it moves the thread to no new phase — finishing /plan is what does that.

team-owned-pr-review.note: The authoritative pull-request review and merge-readiness check, held by the team or initiative surface that owns the work. Clearing it and merging moves the thread work → qa. One person cannot override it: the owning team decides its own readiness.

review.note: The doc-review gate is the Planning->Active gate on all three active boards (plan approved before work goes Active).

work.note: Work (with code-review at the PR boundary) runs in Active on all three active boards.

qa.note: Verify is entered when delivery succeeds, so a card whose stored phase is already qa can still be sitting in the Active column: the acceptance verdict is evaluated against the delivered outcome once the card is in Verify. The entry condition itself is defined once, in the verify_entry block of config/sdlc-schema.json, and is not restated here. CAMPPS gained a separate Verify column on 2026-08-16.

command_classification.description: The in-repository cross-cutting command list and the explicit exclusions (R68): the machine-readable dispositions for routable Saga commands that phase_command_map does not map. Hand-authored; the vendored snapshot is never consulted for these dispositions (R59). REASONS IN THE excluded BLOCK MUST BE FINAL (E10, operator decision 2026-09-07): a placeholder reason - "Excluded pending its own decision" and every variant of it - is not a disposition, and it fails the reason-quality rule in tools/docs/check_adapter.py rather than sitting here unnoticed. A command whose disposition is genuinely undecided belongs in the open-question register, never parked in this block; that rule is what stops the adapter from becoming a second open-question register.
command_classification.completeness_rule: Every routable Saga command resolves into exactly one of three dispositions: mapped to a Stage by phase_command_map, listed in cross_cutting, or listed in excluded. A routable command in none of the three is unclassified and fails the adapter completeness check (tools/docs/check_adapter.py) loudly rather than silently defaulting to no movement. That fail-loud rule is RETAINED for every future command: a snapshot resync or plugin upgrade that adds a routable command must classify it here or the docs gate stays red until an operator ruling classifies it - the rule was never disabled, only satisfied. Amendments to this classification are deliberate register acts, never execution-time inference: the eleven cross-cutting entries were set by the operator's AFK ruling of 2026-08-30, recorded durably on issue infiquetra/infiquetra-sdlc#90, amending R68's landing-time state (issue #92, 2026-08-30) in which the list was empty by recorded choice; each reason below is grounded in that command's own model purpose and ownership boundary, never in the vendored snapshot's phase field (R59).
command_classification.amended_by: Operator AFK ruling, recorded 2026-08-30 on issue infiquetra/infiquetra-sdlc#90 (F-1/KTD9 of the R2 wave review): every currently unclassified routable command is cross-cutting because none independently advances an issue lifecycle Stage - each observes, routes, investigates, controls orchestration, or records learning/direction, while the command it dispatches owns Stage movement.

cross_cutting./delegation-audit: Reconciles the delegation audit store and reports on delegated work: read-only, advisory, invoked on demand and never a gate - the same shape as /fleet-doctor, whose own reason already names it as an owner of recovery actions. It is a skill with no command file at Saga 0.148.0, so a routable-command sweep never finds it; it is named here so that omission is expected rather than a gap. It observes and repairs the delegation record, so no lifecycle Stage moves (E10, operator decision 2026-09-07).
cross_cutting./fleet-doctor: Read-only fleet audit: correlates worktrees, outcome registries, broker leases, chain-verified run facts, dispatch events, and the delegation audit store into finding classes; it owns observation and classification only, while /outcome, the lease broker, teardown, and /delegation-audit own every recovery action - so no lifecycle Stage moves.
cross_cutting./founder-review: Challenges scope, ambition, positioning, timing, and operator risk wherever the operator convenes it; it owns challenge and decision capture, never readiness review or issue movement, so the work it gates advances its own Stage.
cross_cutting./handoff: Prepares a durable transfer envelope for SDLC issue handoff; saga owns the envelope and mission-control owns the issue body, sidecars, labels, board, and GitHub mutation, so the receiving command continues the Stage the sender already reached.
cross_cutting./investigate: Diagnoses the root cause of a bug, failing test, or unexpected behavior before any fix proposal; it owns diagnosis, not shipping, so its findings feed whatever command then moves the Stage.
cross_cutting./loop: Classifies input, finds in-flight work, and dispatches to the command that owns the next phase; it owns routing and the hand-off envelope, never phase work, backend choice, issue filing, deploy, or heavy forensics, so the dispatched command owns Stage movement.
cross_cutting./optimize: Improves a measurable target through bounded one-variable experiments; it owns the experiment loop, not merge or deployment, so no issue leaves its Stage because of it.
cross_cutting./outcome: Coordinates a whole outcome as a durable graph of leaf sagas across issues, above the per-issue run: it routes and dispatches to executors and never runs leaf work itself. Every board write it needs goes through mission-control's submission path - R34 removed its own write authority - and every run transition is the Delivery Manager's, so no lifecycle Stage moves. Recorded as expectation, not as implementation: /outcome is expected to be removed from Saga, that removal is NOT treated as already done, and this adapter describes what runs today; when it is removed the adapter drops it under the existing re-sync checklist (E10, operator decision 2026-09-07, amended).
cross_cutting./pulse: Renders live board, run, run-fact-ledger, and outcome-economics state in one read-only snapshot; it owns rendering while mission-control owns board mutation and saga writers own ticks, so observation moves the record, never the Stage.
cross_cutting./promote: Promotes the select few cross-repo transcendent learnings into infiquetra-context-library as distilled org standards; it owns only the cross-repo journal feed into the context library, not source-repo or SDLC mutation, so the learning outlives the issue without moving any Stage.
cross_cutting./resume: Reconstructs an in-flight work thread in depth and routes it to the owning command; it owns reconstruction and routing, not build/test/PR, so the thread resumes in whichever Stage its owning command holds.
cross_cutting./strategy: Creates or maintains the repository's STRATEGY.md as the durable direction anchor; it owns recording direction while /founder-review challenges it, and direction-setting is a portfolio-level practice that dispatches no issue's Stage movement.
cross_cutting./tier: Sets a run-scoped model/effort tier ceiling or patches a not-yet-run unit's tier mid-run without aborting and re-planning; it writes the override and drives patch/validate/emit without running leaf work, merging, or deploying, so the unit's Stage stays wherever its work put it.
